version.changelog: Refresh public skill metadata for GitHub and ClawHub release sync.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-cws-publisher
Version: 0.2.3

The skill bundle provides a legitimate set of tools for packaging Chrome extensions and preparing release metadata for GitHub and ClawHub. It includes a security-focused script (scan_publish_surface.py) designed to detect accidental leaks of credentials or local paths before publication. The code uses standard subprocess calls for git and gh CLI tools and does not exhibit any signs of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose (packaging a Chrome extension, scanning the repo for publish-time leaks, and rendering release commands); it requests no unexplained credentials and is instruction-only with sensible, focused scripts.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the provided scripts and instructions. Requested binaries (python3, git, gh, clawhub) are relevant to packaging, repo inspection, and rendering publish commands. There are no environment variables or config paths required beyond an optional CWS_PUBLIC_SITE_BASE used to build reviewer-facing links.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the bundled scripts against a user-supplied repo path and to inspect the generated ZIP and leak-scan outputs. The scripts operate on files tracked by git (falling back to all files) and will read many textual files to detect token-shaped strings and other patterns; they then write JSON/MD outputs. This is appropriate for a publish-audit tool, but those outputs may contain excerpts of any discovered secrets or paths, so users should treat them as sensitive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only). All code is present in the skill bundle; nothing is downloaded or extracted at install time, which minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require credentials or environment variables, only optionally reads CWS_PUBLIC_SITE_BASE to build reviewer links. Scripts use subprocess.run which inherits the agent environment when they execute child processes — this is normal but means any local credentials in the environment could be visible to commands (git/gh/npx) executed by the agent. The skill itself does not request or store secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable. It does not request permanent system presence or modify other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent for packaging and auditing Chrome extensions, but take a few precautions before running it: 1) Point it only at the repo path you intend to publish — the scripts will read many tracked files and write JSON/Markdown outputs that may contain excerpts of anything matched (including token-like strings). 2) Review the generated leak-scan output before sharing it; treat those artifacts as potentially sensitive. 3) The rendered publish commands will call gh and run an npx clawhub publish command — do not run them unless you intend to create a public repo/release and have the appropriate GitHub/ClawHub credentials. 4) If you want reviewer-facing links to point to a public site rather than repo blobs, set CWS_PUBLIC_SITE_BASE. 5) Confirm any repo-local reviewer_gate scripts (scripts/reviewer_gate.py or .githooks/pre-push) before overriding their behavior. Overall the skill appears to do what it claims, but follow normal caution when executing repository-modifying or publishing commands.
